chunks: Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked him about salat (prayer) during the night and the day when the sun, the moon, and the stars cannot be seen, so he said:
"You exert your judgment and deliberately determine the qiblah to the best of your ability."

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, a natural indicator for orientation
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act whose direction is being determined
key_terms.النُّجُومُ: the stars, visible markers for navigation and orientation
key_terms.الْقَمَرُ: the moon, a celestial sign used for direction
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the qiblah, the direction faced in salat (prayer)
key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ: during the night, when usual visual signs may be absent
key_terms.تَجْتَهِدُ: you exert effort and judgment in determining the proper direction
key_terms.وَالنَّهَارِ: during the day, likewise covering all times of prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do to determine the qiblah when the sun, moon, and stars are not visible?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for determining the qiblah when visible celestial signs are unavailable. It instructs the worshipper to use personal effort and reasoned judgment to face the qiblah as best as possible.
